verdict.tagline: A dark cabin deckbuilder that transforms into something entirely unexpected.
for_you_if: you enjoy deckbuilders that radically change shape
you like solving room escape puzzles
not_for_you_if: you dislike heavy reliance on random generation
you want a consistent gameplay style throughout
you get frustrated by punishing achievement grinds

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Early players find a challenging deckbuilder that shifts styles after the opening act alongside puzzle elements.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game changes its style and mechanics significantly after the first act, transitioning away from the initial cabin setting and roguelike deckbuilder format.

citations.review_text:
I can't really reccomend this game. 

It does what it set out to do which is be a psuedo-horror exploration and puzzle game with heavy narrative that uses a basic card game as a vehicle for storytelling. 

I respect the devs for that sticking with their vision, but it's not really what I was buying the game for (I wanted a card game as the sole focus with a strong narrative to tie it all together). 

The puzzles are not very hard but can be a bit interesting. The story is ok, not really my cup of tea past Act 1. The parts of the game I really enjoyed got rug-pulled away after going into act 2.

TL;DR This game would be an instant recommend if the devs had scrapped Act 2 & 3 as well as the ARG elements and instead poured their efforts into making Act 1 longer & with more content.

Act 1 is exactly what you think it is, a neat roguelike deckbuilder with fantastic theming and interesting puzzles alongside the deckbuilder that expand the game out dramatically. I can't recommend Act 1 enough. But it's quite short, I beat it in about 3 hours. Then the slog begins. 

Act 2 is an 8-bit card battler, nothing like the game you were playing before in theming.  Like if halfway though a horror movie they played an entire unbroken episode of Pokemon. Completley kills the pace and made me lose interest in the game.

Act 3 is a return to formula, now you're trapped in a factory instead of a creepy cabin. P03 isn't as interesting an opponent as Leshy, so it's not as fun or interesting. 

The finale is interesting, but it doesn't make up for everything else. 

The devs appear to be familiar with the phrase "kill your darlings," considering that the core mechanic of act 1 is just that. But they should have looked at their own game and cut cut cut all the bloat they added on. It's disappointing and could have been done much better.

The game changes so majorly after Act 1 that I completely lost interest. The setting, atmosphere, art style, mechanics, and mystery/intrigue of the cabin really hooked me, and it would've been wonderful if the game was a continuation or expansion of that. Normally I hate roguelike elements, but I was so hooked I wanted to keep going. And then it's all gone. While I can appreciate a nice meta-narrative, they tend to tow the line between being mind blowing or pretentious, and Inscryption fell into the latter. It tries to be 3 different games in one, rather than stick to anything it builds up. I'm so disappointed, this was shaping up to be one of the best games I've played in a long time.

I think this is the first game I've ever bought that becomes something else after two hours. And not in a pleasant or fun or smart way.

If I have to describe this game quickly is "the stealth section in an fps game, but that stealth section is 50% of the game".

I don't know exactly how to describe the feeling, I feel like I've been cheated by what I saw in the Steam store images and the game description. That's not the game, pure and simple.
Everything you see in the store page it's... the first couple of hours, on a slow pace, after that the game changes all the rules and you are playing a different, extremely boring and lame, thing.
I was really excited in the first part of the game and then....

The premise of a deckbuilder roguelite falls very quickly in mostly boring puzzle solving and repetition that almost all the times can be only solved with rng. 
Didn't pick a defense against air monsters? Sorry, restart the game. Not the single "act", the entire game. 
The explode bot is not in the right position? Retry untill it is (but hope you have the right cards now). 

You really really really have the feelings that there is the "right" way to play the game, when you have decisions to make, and the "wrong" way. And that you will be punished if you'll pick the dev's not intended path.
This feeling is not felt for the first part of the game but becomes unbearable after the first "game switch". 
And no, re-doing the entirety of the first part of the game just because I followed "my" way is not an option. This is not a decision heavy rpg.

The mystery and the plotline is... interesting for sure but it surely isn't worth the time. This game absolutely do not respect your time. I know there are people that have a kick for doing the same repettive things for horus and hours for a 1% chance of getting a different result, but this is not what I wanted to buy and this is absolutely not what they are selling.

This game is nice.

To review it properly i'll have to spoil a twist that happens after around 2 hours of game, because this twist doesn't affect only the story, but the gameplay as well. So if you wanna go in blindly, i'll just say the game is worth it, but the change after 2 hours can be frustrating if you're expecting a pure creepy roguelike deckbuilder, so be aware.

[spoiler]The game has 3 acts, each of them have their own gameplay style and mechanics.
The first act is a creepy roguelike deckbuilder where you do short runs and try to progress in the story by interacting with the cabin where you are trapped, it's simple, it has a dark and mysterious vibe, the cards and the enviroment are more rudimentary, with paper cards and board, and it's short, around 2 hours and you will be out of the cabin and on the second act.[/spoiler]

[spoiler]The second act is trash... just kidding. The second act turns the game into a 2D pixelated pokémon-esque adventure, where you roam around a continent collecting cards to build your deck and defeating a few minions and then bosses to progress. This changes the game completely and can threw some people away. It almost threw me away, but i stuck around and ended up enjoying it, but not as much as the first act.
This act is a bit longer, for introducing lots of new mechanics, like energy and orbs, and cards. It took me around 5 hours to finish it.[/spoiler]

[spoiler]Then there's the third act. Where you go back to a scenario just like the cabin, but larger, metalic and technnological, with a hologram board and cards similar to floppy disks. The gameplay changes to something more similar to the roguelike style, as you advancing room by room, but now you're only doing one big run where you can keep your upgrades and cards, and if you die, you respawn at a checkpoint and only lose a few minutes of progress.
It took me around 3 hours to finish this section and then the game.[/spoiler]

[spoiler]For those who don't wanna play the second…

A simple rogue-like deckbuilder that builds into something compelling through atmosphere, a cryptic meta-narrative, and game-changing plot twists. Act 1 slowly drew me in, building intrigue and tension. After Act 1, I felt like the game lost some steam. The mechanics mainly stay the same regarding the card-playing portions of the game, but it has lost the charm of the first act and the extra game mechanics introduced become tedious. Overall, though, I enjoyed the gameplay loop and found the story emotionally moving by the end.

I LOVED the first act of this game, and it was also the only thing I saw of the game before buying it, and when I finished act 1, and act 2 begun, I lost all my interest in it, and as a blessing and a curse, I finished act 1 fast enough that I was able to refund the game. I just wish the game was more act 1, and as much as I'm happy I got to experience and truly enjoy the first act, I knew I was not going to enjoy the rest of the game, even more so after watching videos of it.

I highly recommend this game for it's first act, but there was nothing shown of anything afterwards, you're lead to believe act 1 is the game, and I felt insanely miss-lead when I finished act 1 and there was game I didn't want to play, game I didn't purchase. I have to not recommend this game because if I wasn't able to refund this game, I would have felt incredibly burned. As amazing as act 1 was, it was not worth the amount I paid for it, and if I couldn't refund it, it would spend the rest of my life rotting away in my steam library, never seeing the light of day again.

Please do some research into the later acts of this game before you buy it, if I had done so I wouldn't have bought it in the first place.

Pains me to leave a bad review, but the game is a bit misleading. The First act of the game is exactly as advertised, retro style graphics, 3d card game mechanics. And so on. Once you complete this act, which is basically the demo. You leave the cabin and restart the game as a 2d Pixel Art card game. While the game plays similar, all of the charm is completely lost and its essentially as if another developer reskinned the game. They do not show photos of this part of the game in the steam page, and because it took me 4 hours to get through act 1, i cannot refund the game. 

The art style and everything in acts 2 and 3 are essentially a poorly designed, ugly pixel art game. You'll have to look up spoilers of the game to see for yourself.

This game is absolutely unlike anything I have ever played before. It features card game elements as well as board game elements. The tension is non-stop, and every single round feels different; you learn from game to game, constantly encountering new characters, creatures, or enemies. Along the way, you meet various figures who may or may not have good intentions.

It is a fantastic journey where you play against a figure that is hard to describe. The entire game is incredibly atmospheric and cohesive. While the story is being told to you, you live through it, all while sitting in an old, dark cabin filled with many items to explore and use. Sounds weird? It is—and yet everything makes perfect sense.

Kudos to the developers! This game is something totally different, yet it pulls you into an oddly familiar environment and completely captivates you. You will make sacrifices—many sacrifices—and every single decision has its consequences.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as difficult and challenging, particularly when starting out or facing strict defeat conditions.

citations.review_text: I don't even know how to review this game. Just play it blind with no spoilers. Who knows how deep it goes. This is not just one game, or even three games. Actually mind bending. Keep in mind that if you aren't good at deck-builders it will be really hard when you're starting out. Just stick with it and push through the first part, trust.
I have enjoyed some card games before, used to play Hearthstone before the updates were just too much to keep up, this game is a dark and challenging one, it is very enjoyable.

This is an absolute banger of a game! 



It's definitely a bit difficult, especially in the beginning, notably if you're "one of the dumber ones" like me, the game is still very fun to play! You get to know and understand the rules by simply playing the game, what i really like. Which greatly confused me at first, but the more you play, the more everything makes sense, you start to develop strategies, and it gets more enjoyable by the second! Even when I get so frustrated I quit and take a break, it's never for long, it's just that fun! 



This is definitely one of my favorite games now! I truly feel blessed that I got to witness this absolutely scrumptious game. I highly recommend it!

this game is really really REALLY good. like excessively good almost. its fantastic both story wise and gameplay wise, and it is so shockingly good with what it does, what it changes up, and what it keeps- the characters are really well written, and this game is best gone in blind.

there are a few drastic artstyle changes and gameplay changes that  can be a bit jarring, however the central card gameplay mostly stays the same, and if you only end up liking the first part of the game theres an extended mode for more first act gameplay. Highly suggest you get it while its on sale or just whenever, geninuely its fantastic and worth all of the money. 

Despite what some negative reviews say, this was the first game i played by Daniel Mullins Games, and I think its great both with zero context as well as with the full story. Please play it!! im so serious!!

This game is amazing. When I originally bought and installed it after playing the demo, I was expecting /only/ what the demo gave you; a deckbuilding game with some exploration features and limited lore. Now, having played the full game (all three acts + the finale), I can tell you it's so much more than that. The lore in this game is absolutely fantastic and is so interesting. I love the details of Magnificus and P03 in card-form talking to you, and I love their rivalry. Also have to like the barely confirmed yaoi:,). Even though, for me, act 3 was a little bit unexciting (I originally bought the game because I liked the cozy style of the demo, and act 3 took that away), it was still a really well-made and fun to play game. I loved the use of different styles; first, the cozy-with-subtle-horror-aspects for act one, then the 8-bit gameplay of act two, the robotic feel of act three, and finally the combination of it all plus a little more (Magnificus and Grimora's playthrough). Overall, a 10/10 game and I would absolutely recommend to others. Can't stop playing it!!

The battle deckbuilding gameplay is satisfying, especially when you discover loopholes. I was hooked by the escape-room vibe of part 1, found the NES gameplay of part 2 rather flat, but then part 3 really felt high-stakes. Really enjoyed how creepy Luke's story was too!

The game forces you to mess with 2 of the 4 decks, and I used the 2nd Act to try out Grimora's deck as well. Magnificus' deck is the least realized of the 4 lacking a comparable amount of strategy variety - and the only reason for this is that his deck needs to be experienced (and it's heavily implied) in a first-person keller synth dark fantasy Les Legions Noires raw xeroxed cover tape black metal role-playing FMV dungeon crawler gameplay setting and this comment is an open call to KGB to continue Moloch worship blood sacrifices so that Kola superdeep borehole may emanate this hypothetical game on a VHS tape some day as well.

[h1] What is this game? [/h1]
Inscryption is the indirect successor to "The Hex" and "Pony Island" - expanding upon the ARG Mullins-verse. 
This game has you play as Luke 'The Lucky Carder' - a youtuber who happens to stumble upon a mysterious floppy disk that seems to have a will of its own. 

[h2] Price/replay value [/h2]
Horrible - Bad - Decent - Good - [u] Amazing [/u]

[h2] Achievement hunting [/h2]
Akin to Mullins games - there's [i] a ton [/i] of missables and secret related ones. A lot of these can be quite challenging, but not impossibly difficult with a guide and proper setup.
By far and large the hardest are Kaycee's mod related - having you go through a gauntlet of challenging (and often unfair) fights to barely scrape your way to victory. Skull storm especially is the hardest by miles.

[h2] Pros/cons [/h2]
[b] Pros [/b]
[list]
[*]Tons of replay value (Kaycee's mod is a roguelike mode)
[*]Tons of secrets and an entire ARG (granted solved by now)
[*]Solid story with fun characters
[/list]

[b] Cons [/b]
[list]
[*]Kaycee's mod can get very rng heavy
[*]Fair hand mechanic makes most 1 blood cards unplayable
[/list]

[h2] Overall opinion [/h2]
I thoroughly enjoyed this game. I played through the main story a few years ago and had a blast uncovering all the secrets and little extras. Recently picked it back up to finish Kaycee's mod, and whilst it wasn't always "fair" - I did still enjoy most runs and overall would say the game retains its replayability and overall enjoyment. It's also fun to see what broken combos you can make in the main acts as this game allows you to do a lot of silly stuff. 
Highly recommend to all the patient gamers who haven't played it yet.

[h2] tldr; [/h2]
Fun puzzle card game with wacky balancing.

[h2] Should you buy it? [/h2] 
Highly recommend you do.

citations.review_text:
I got this game simply because i saw about 10 minutes of gameplay on Markiplier's channel, it peaked my interest and i went to play it myself. I had never even played a card based video game up until now, but something about the setting and environment just looked like i can't pass up on it

It sure was worth it, Inscryption easily became one of my favorite games i have ever played. The gameplay is fun, easy to learn and well taught by design. Losing never felt frustrating even if i had got far, each new run usually introduced something new to help you along the way and/or it was a chance to test out different Decks and Cards you may not fully understand yet. Experimenting and theorizing what certain cards and abilities really do was fun, as not every creature was always as simple and straightforward as it first seemed. Especially the rulebook which intentionally has a few pages partially blacked out leaving you to theorize, test and figure out how strong that one Sigil really is

All this great gameplay is also supported by an interesting story, environment and world. The cabin puzzles are fun and fairly easy to solve, always advancing the story and rewarding you with more options.

I would get into it more but i don't wanna go spoiling anything. I'll just say that this whole game, just like some of the cards.. is a lot more then what it first appears to be on the surface

The battle deckbuilding gameplay is satisfying, especially when you discover loopholes. I was hooked by the escape-room vibe of part 1, found the NES gameplay of part 2 rather flat, but then part 3 really felt high-stakes. Really enjoyed how creepy Luke's story was too!
escape room vibes and a fun card game.  Why does Act 1 feel like the best and main part of the game?

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the final achievements in Kaycee's mod require a significant time investment and can feel like a grind.

citations.review_text: I love everything about inscryption kaycees mod achievements are the only thing in this game that is awful cuz that last beat with all challenges mods is an insane timesink for one achievement xD but i love this game you should play it for sure

You already know what Inscryption is - one of the most inventive and thoughtfully-designed games I've ever played. The story feels a little incomplete without whatever arg elements are popular these days, but it's good enough to take you through three (4? 5?) different deckbuilders without boring you. Plus, for fans of the rougelike genre, there's a good few dozen hours of refreshingly creative concepts, rebalanced and remixed into a difficult and satisfying (if grindy towards the end) challenge. Absolutely recommend.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that Kaycee's mod can experience high randomness or RNG issues during later fights.

citations.review_text: very fun, but the postgame is a bit unbalanced. The later fights in Kacee's mod are sometimes unwinnable (eg. double strike turkey vulture on turn 1 and you draw a pelt) unless you have set up a guaranteed win strategy. Don't let that stop you from playing though, as the main game is VERY polished and fair.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players highlight initial cabin exploration and drastic mechanical shifts, alongside punishing late achievements.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a cabin setting where players can explore the room and are rewarded for doing so during the opening act.

citations.review_text:
I remember playing the gamejam version of this a long time ago, the theme was "sacrifice", it was well received and turned into a full game. It went from a simple 20 minutes card game to a full deckbuilding roguelike, with way more cards and decks you can play and ways you can improve your playstyle. The story was also expanded and the theme of sacrifice isn't as prominent anymore.

The game starts really intriguing, act 1 has such a good atmosphere, the mystery of what is going on and how are you going to win against such big odds keeps you moving forward... you can explore the cabin and the game rewards you for doing so. The soundtrack and sounds fits the ambience well, I think this game is really immersive. And when you think you're done the game continues.. this part I didn't like much but the core of the game which is the cardgame is really fun to play.

Act I of the game was really good, but then they decided to make a new game following it in Act II and just when i learned the mechanics of the game, i suddenly need to learn some new mechanics of some new game. Act III tries to remedy this by bringing the player back to the room with a table of cards, but this time again new mechanics and a more boring digital world, instead of the mysterious beast theme of Act I. It tries to tie it all together with some lackluster horror/mystery theme, but without actually thinking about the card mechanics, it feels more like a glue on than any real stakes in the game. During the gameplay it's never explained how the opponent can just slap more and more cards and never care about the blood/bone/energy mechanics and the last few goodbye games in the end have no meaning whatsoever, since you can only win no matter what you choose, you are forced to only click on and listen to the story. It feels like the game was made for the developer to tell their story instead of thinking about the player.

citations.review_text: Such an amazing game. Novel creativity and talented execution is a hard combo to find. No notes.

[spoiler] i like how in act 1 you need to have all these op upgrades to beat the game, while in kayse's mod you have understood the game mechanics enough, to beat the game, not just without the upgrades, but with extra challanges aswell [/spoiler]

If you love games with a dark twist, this game is for you. An engaging card game that pulls you in and surrounds you in its world. If you get bored of one version, you can just continue in the story and the game will completely change while still keeping the fun card gameplay. From hidden ARGs to annoying woodland critters, this game really does have it all for a card game.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the final achievement requiring grizzly boss fights with strict skull restrictions and one candle is excessively difficult and frustrating.

citations.review_text:
I love the main game, I enjoyed Kaycee's mod a lot, I think Inscryption is absolutely brilliant, though I'm sad about Grimora not getting more screen time--however, don't try to 100% this damn game. I mean it. 

Spoiler: 

||Grizzly boss fights with one candle and every other skull restriction in place for that stupid final achievement is so hard, it's genuinely not fun anymore, and that's what finally made me stop after beating challenge level 12 and trying to progress to that point. I've done at least a few dozen runs trying to get the right combination for defeating the first bosses, trying to grind up to get that last achievement and it just doesn't happen. When literally every battle on the board is so nail-bitingly, teeth-pullingly hard because the actual mechanics of the game are overwritten with pure punishment, it's just too much. It stops being the game I was enjoying and just becomes a form of self torture. Anyone who managed the achievement has to be either absurdly masochistic, has the most incredible luck imaginable, is actually cheating somehow, or knows something I and most other players clearly don't. Congrats, Kaycee, you beat me, now gtfo.||

Finally 100%'d the game and it was SOOOOOOOOOOO worth it. I had taken some time off bc of the final achievement, so much has to go your way and getting a run going can take time, but I finally sat down and did it. I can't recommend this game enough, please play this game. You'll enjoy it
